stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its velocity vector at time t seconds is \( v(t) = \left\langle 3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)},\ 3 t^{2} - 6 \right\rangle \), with velocity measured in feet per second. Using a calculator, find the total distance, in feet, traveled by the particle over the time interval \( 0 \le t \le 3 \). Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The speed of the particle is the magnitude of its velocity, \( \lVert v(t) \rVert = \sqrt{\left(3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^2 + \left(3 t^{2} - 6\right)^2} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: speed as the magnitude of velocity

worked_solution.text: The total distance is the integral of speed over the interval, \( \int_{0}^{3} \sqrt{\left(3 \cos{\left(2 t \right)}\right)^2 + \left(3 t^{2} - 6\right)^2}\,dt \), which a calculator gives as about 22.048 feet.
worked_solution.rule_named: total distance as the integral of speed

options.derivation: distance written as two separate one-dimensional distances added together, the integral of |x'(t)| plus the integral of |y'(t)|
the net change in position reported, the length of the displacement vector from the integrals of the two components
the speed written without its square root, so the integrand is x'(t)^2 + y'(t)^2
